Flooding Forces Closures and Evacuations at Canadian Hospitality Industry Sites

A series of severe storms has triggered widespread flooding in southern British Columbia, causing significant disruption across the Canadian hospitality industry. As rivers overflow and heavy rains persist, several hotels, resorts, and conference centres have been forced to close temporarily, with ongoing evacuations and property damage reported.

The deluge, which began late last week and is still unfolding, has inundated basements, lobbies, and ground-floor amenities in affected facilities. Staff at the Valley Vista Resort in the Fraser River region were evacuated early Sunday morning due to rapidly rising waters. "Safety is our top priority," said site manager Linda Chou. "We have moved all guests and staff to higher ground, but the extent of the damage is still being assessed." At least 120 employees are unable to return to work at the resort pending further notice.

Elsewhere, the downtown Riverside Inn in Hope has sustained water damage to 30 guest rooms and communal areas. "We’ve never seen flooding like this," said operations director Karim Patel. "Our maintenance team is working around the clock to protect essential equipment and minimize losses."

According to the Canadian Hospitality Industry Council, at least 18 sites in the province have reported partial or full closures, with hundreds of workers temporarily displaced. "The immediate concern is for the safety and welfare of staff and on-site guests," said Council spokesperson Rhonda Macleod. "Many properties face extensive cleanup and repairs, and some may be closed for weeks, depending on the severity of the flooding."

Analysts warn that the ongoing nature of the event makes it difficult to estimate the full impact. "These facilities are particularly vulnerable to flooding due to their riverside locations," said industry analyst Jean-Paul Tremblay. "With more rain forecast, there is a risk that conditions could worsen."

The situation remains fluid, with hospitality operators monitoring weather updates and prioritizing emergency procedures as flooding continues.
